THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH THE  STATION HOUSE OFFICER POLICE STATION JATARA  DISTRICT TIKAMGARH (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI SANTOSH YADAV - DY. GOVT. ADVOCATE AND SHRI ANURAG
PRAJAPATI - ADVOCATE FOR THE OBJECTOR/VICTIM)

This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.377/2022, dated 30.12.2022, registered at Police Station - Jatara, District Tikamgarh (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 450,
323, 376, 506 of IPC.
Applicant is in detention since 19.01.2023.
2. As per the prosecution story, on 30.12.2022, 40 years old prosecutrix, a mother of three children lodged an FIR about commission of rape upon her by the applicant at 8:30 P.M. on 29.12.2022.
It was also alleged that he beat her by kicks and fists and thereafter fled away from there.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.

He is having old enmity with the prosecutrix and her Ankit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4178992/
1 family.

sentences.text: Earlier in the year 2017, prosecutrix had lodged a false FIR against him about causing marpeet but later that matter ended into compromise.
It is further submitted that FIR has been lodged on the next day almost after a delay of 18 hours, whereas distance of the Police Station from the place of occurrence is only 12 kilometers.
It is further submitted that applicant is working in a private firm "Om Construction" at Bhadodra (Gujarat) and on the alleged date of occurrence he was not in the village.
He was at Bhadodara (Gujarat).
In support of his argument attendance sheet of Om Construction Company has been filed in which his presence, on 29.12.2022, is shown at Bhadodara (Gujarat).
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the objector as well as learned counsel for the State have opposed the grant of bail to the applicant contending that the Annexeure A/5 attendance sheet has been issued by a private company and no sanctity can be attached with it.
Therefore, they have prayed for rejection of the bail application.

5 . Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case and considering applicant's submission about his presence at Bhadodara (Gujarat) on the date of incident, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

However, learned counsel for the State is directed to forward Annexure A/5 document to the concerned Police Station and to get the same verified from the company about applicant's presence there on 29.12.2022.

Applicant - Ankit be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
6.
However, it is made clear that if Annexure A/5 attendance sheet is not found true then this order will become ineffective and applicant shall surrender then and there before the trial Court.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case o f bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE Jasleen Ankit vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4178992/
